question: Can you upgrade a wastewater plant's switchgear?
html:
Yes. Electrical work at treatment plants and pump stations is central to our Connecticut wastewater business. That business came to us with Horton Electrical Services in September 2026 (CET growth plan). Our data tracks plant projects rather than switchgear line items, so we would confirm scope on a site walk.

What we bring

  • Electrical crews based in Worcester, Taunton and Norwell, MA, and Canton, CT (CET growth plan).
  • Licensing in six states (CET growth plan).
  • Roughly 260–290 people after the Horton deal, est. (CET public filings).
  • NuWave efficiency work. It fits plants with large energy loads, such as aeration (CET wastewater-plant targets).

Plant projects we're tracking

PlantFunded or listed workFurther requests
New Haven East Shore, CT$82M wet-weather and odor-control upgrade$19.2M process-air compressors
Hartford WPCF, CT$24.3M sludge screening and equalization$31.6M Island Road and Hog Brook pump stations
Norwalk WPCF, CT$26M final-settling-tank upgrade$48M aeration system
MWRA Deer Island, MA$289M Clarifier #2none listed

Source: CET wastewater-plant targets.

Some caveats on these figures:

  • Connecticut "request" items are not on the fundable list. Only Table 2 or Category I items are (CET wastewater-plant targets).
  • Our data does not show which of these projects include switchgear replacement. The bid documents and engineer's specifications would answer that.
  • Deer Island already generates 26% of its own power. The fit there is electrical subcontracting plus storage and efficiency work (CET wastewater-plant targets).

What helps us scope it

  • Single-line diagrams and the age and ratings of the existing gear.
  • Allowable outage windows. Plants must keep treating flow during the work.
  • Funding status and procurement route for the project.
  • Whether you want ongoing monitoring or maintenance after the upgrade.

We don't advise on permits or regulatory obligations. Your engineer and regulator own those questions.

Each plant electrical job opens a relationship that can lead to the 62 funded or requested projects Horton is aimed at. It can also lead to the recurring monitoring and service contracts the growth plan relies on to lift CET's value (CET growth plan).

Next actions

  1. Pull bid documents for New Haven, Hartford and Norwalk. Flag any switchgear or electrical distribution scope.
  2. Write a one-page wastewater electrical capability sheet with Horton project references. The current data has none.
  3. Add a field to the target list marking switchgear or power-distribution scope for each of the 183 facilities.
  4. Pair each switchgear bid with a NuWave efficiency review and a monitoring or maintenance option.
